newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour party loses high tax image - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour party loses high tax image - survey.

text.p: British voters believe taxation under a Labour government would be only slightly higher than under a Conservative government, a poll said on Wednesday.

The survey, conducted by the Financial Times newspaper and advertising agency FCB, found voters who had not yet decided where to place their vote felt the Conservative government no longer deserved to be seen as a low-tax party.

The Financial Times said the findings were based on discussions with 72 focus group members in three marginal British constituencies. It said undecided voters -- whom both political parties are trying to cultivate ahead of Britain's general election -- were prepared to accept Labour's claim the Conservative government planned to put value-added tax on food if it was re-elected.
But voters also said the Labour party was "always changing its mind" and "preoccupied with just getting into power".
The Financial Times said British Prime Minister John Major would decide this week whether to hold the election on March 20 or stick to the original timetable of May 1.
